rows.label: Token following "Capital" in finance terms
rows.description: Fires on continuation tokens right after the word "Capital" (e.g. " As" in "Capital Asset", " Bud", " and"), mostly in title-case finance headings. Silent on " As" when it is not preceded by "Capital".

members.label: Word-start fragments in Title Case (unclear)
members.description: Fires on capitalized word-initial tokens (Success, Under, Know, Tem) in Title-Cased text, often where a longer word continues; the logit effect is mixed, so it is unclear.

members.label: Title-case word-start fragment (unclear)
members.description: Fires on capitalized word-initial fragments (Fre, Ge, Th, Es) in Title Case headline-like text, where a word is split into pieces; logits are mixed, so unclear.

members.label: Title-case word-start fragments (unclear)
members.description: Fires on capitalized word-start fragments (Fre, Ge, Th, Es) beginning a split word in Title Case headline-like text; peaks vary and logits are weak, so unclear.

rows.label: Control word detector
rows.description: Fires on the word "control" (Control, control, controls), strongest in "Traffic Control Systems" and as a noun or verb in technical or management text. Members are mostly token detectors for control variants.

members.label: Token " control"
members.description: Fires only on the token " control" (e.g., "control strategies", "control procedures"), in technical/engineering contexts. Logits mildly boost control-related continuations like "Control", "over", "acy"; evidence is thin.

members.label: Token " Control"
members.description: Fires only on the token " Control" (e.g., "Control Systems", "Control materials"), in technical/engineering text. Logits mildly boost " Control"/" control" variants; evidence is thin.

members.label: Title-case word starts (unclear)
members.description: Fires on scattered capitalized word-start tokens (Str, Tem, Other, Our) in title-case text; peaks are mixed, and logits favor word-fragment continuations like Tw, pol, Kos. Unclear.

rows.label: Cell division terms (chrom, pol, II)
rows.description: Fires on word pieces in cell-division (mitosis/meiosis) text: ' chrom' in chromatids/chromosomes, ' pol' in poles, ' II' after phase names. Predicts biology word endings. Silent in physics/abstract text.

members.label: ' chrom' word-start token
members.description: Fires only on the token " chrom" as a word fragment in chromatography, chromatid, chromosome, chromatin. Logits boost continuations like atin, omer, atch, ission.

members.label: "fect" in "Perfect" tense headings
members.description: Fires on the token "fect" in "Per|fect" within grammar headings like "Past/Future/Conditional Perfect Continuous". Logits are mixed and unclear, with weak boosts for '-' and ' ('.

members.label: Arabic mid-word letters (unclear)
members.description: Fires on mid-word Arabic letters (ة, ن, و) and occasionally Japanese ク or repeated commas; peaks are scattered, with no clear shared meaning and weak logits.

rows.label: ' men' in "menstrual"
rows.description: Fires on ' men' as the first piece of "menstrual" (and weakly on ' Race' in "Arms Race"), i.e. a word-initial fragment inside a longer word. Circuit is failed and diffuse, with only generic members.

members.label: Mid-word fragments, unclear
members.description: Fires on varied mid-word or noun/adjective tokens (ative, pro, scene, balance, id, fier) in descriptive prose; peaks are inconsistent. Logits weakly favor ' of'. Unclear.

members.label: Word after "the" (unclear)
members.description: Fires on mixed tokens, often word pieces or nouns/adjectives right after "the" (cout, lish, ree, risk, principal, expression); peaks are inconsistent. Weakly boosts " of" next.

members.label: Mixed tokens, unclear (further/later)
members.description: Fires on mid-word or mixed tokens (' operation', 'aren', 'つ', ' IN') with no coherent pattern; weakly promotes adverbs like 'further', 'later', 'additional', 'moreover'.

rows.label: "not limited to" negated limitation
rows.description: Fires on ' limited' (also 'restricted', 'confined') right after a negation, as in "is not limited to", where a "not limited to..." construction is expected. Weaker for "but not limited to" and "mostly restricted to".

members.label: Token " limited"
members.description: Fires solely on the token " limited" (adjective, as in "limited to", "limited allusions"). Logits weakly favor " access", " limited", " space", " edition", but the evidence is thin and mixed.

members.label: "not limited to" phrase
members.description: Fires on " limited" (occasionally " restricted") right after "not" in "is not limited to…" constructions; logits show no clear next-token pattern.

members.label: Negated verb "do not contain/have"
members.description: Fires on verbs or nouns (contain, have, elements) right after a negation ("does not contain", "no particular elements"); logits mildly favor nor/except/unless/instead, but evidence is sparse.

rows.label: food token detector
rows.description: Fires on the word "food"/"Food", strongest on repeated "Food and X" headings and on food in regulatory or sustainability phrases. Predicts follow-ons like security, service, handling. Members are mostly food-token detectors.

members.label: "red" in ingredient (food prep)
members.description: Fires on the "red" subtoken inside "ingredient(s)" and once on " plate", in food and cooking contexts. It pushes up prep, prepared, presentation and allergen tokens. The evidence is thin, so this is somewhat unclear.

members.label: Grill/barbecue word fragments (food)
members.description: Fires on mid-word subword pieces in grilling/barbecue words (gr-ill, gr-illed, barbec-ue) in food-description contexts; logits favor cooking/food continuations like cook, taste, restaurant.

members.label: Token " food" before noun
members.description: Fires only on the token " food" in food safety/industry contexts. Logits favor following nouns like security, supply, trade, safety, service.

rows.label: Connectors in lists of consequences
rows.description: Fires on connectors and words (' and', ',', ' economic', 'ism', ' in') inside lists of negative consequences or effects (hardship, instability, unrest) in historical or social cause-and-effect text. Silent on ' and' joining ordinary nouns or topics.

members.label: Predicts negative-consequence words
members.description: Fires on mixed tokens (" only", " can", ",", " communication") in expository text about problems, where a negative-outcome word (mis-, incorrect, errors, poor) comes next. Peaks are diverse; somewhat unclear.

members.label: Subject before past-tense verb
members.description: Fires on the end of a subject noun phrase in historical or explanatory text about a concept, where a past-tense verb like "were developed", "became", or "was introduced" comes next. Peak tokens are mixed.

members.label: Humanism/Renaissance context function words
members.description: Fires on function words (of, for, the, comma) in passages about humanism and the Renaissance period; logits favor historical verbs like began/became/were, suppress must/provides. Peaks are mixed, so unclear.

rows.label: Structure nouns followed by that/can
rows.description: Fires on relative pronouns or modals/infinitive 'to' (that, can, could, which, to) right after a noun for built structures or buildings, in engineering text, where a verb about structural function (withstand, support, reach) comes next. Silent on 'that' in non-engineering clauses.

members.label: Engineering-context function words (unclear)
members.description: Fires on mixed connectives (' and', ' to', ',') in engineering/structure-related text; promotes 'engineering/engine/engineer' as next token. Peaks are inconsistent, so somewhat unclear.

members.label: Composite materials engineering context (unclear)
members.description: Fires on function words like " of", " in", " remarkable" in intros about composite/engineered materials; predicts materials-engineering words (mechanical, manufact, materials, designs). Mixed tokens, so somewhat unclear.

members.label: Plural subject, predicts plural verb
members.description: Fires on commas, "these", and "),", typically right after a plural subject noun phrase, where a plural verb or pronoun comes next; boosts " are", " were", " they" and suppresses singular "its/his".

rows.label: "global" as modifier
rows.description: Fires on the word "global" (also "Global", "international", "-wide") used as a modifier, often before nouns like environmental, economy or issues. Predicts cooperation-type continuations. Silent on the contrast text, which has no such modifier.

members.label: Capitalized " Global" at title start
members.description: Fires on the token " Global", seen at the start of a document or heading (e.g. "Global Transportation Systems"). Logits push suffixes like -ization/-ized and scale/citizens. Evidence is thin, with only 6 examples.

members.label: Growing awareness → environment
members.description: Fires on "growing", "of", "the" in phrases like "growing concerns/awareness of the…" in environmental-movement text; logits boost "Environment"/"environment" next, so it predicts environmental topics.

members.label: Pre-"international/global" context words
members.description: Fires on function words like " beyond" and " the" in globalization/international-relations text, where the next word is likely "international", "global", or "abroad"; evidence is thin and mixed.
